index.html.Mars – Understanding the Planet, Its Dan: Marte: comprender el planeta, sus peligros y la importancia de la supervivencia
index.html.Mars, known as the Red Planet, is one of: Marte, conocido como el Planeta Rojo, es uno de los cuerpos celestes que más interés ha despertado en la exploración espacial por sus características geológicas, atmosféricas y ambientales. Es el cuarto planeta desde el Sol y uno de los principales objetivos de las futuras misiones de exploración humana. Sin embargo, aunque comparte algunas similitudes con la Tierra, sus condiciones naturales son extremadamente distintas y plantean grandes retos para la supervivencia.
index.html.To understand what it would be like to l: Para entender cómo sería vivir en Marte es necesario conocer su composición química y su estructura interna, además de sus principales características físicas. Su superficie está formada sobre todo por rocas, minerales y polvo rico en óxidos de hierro, responsables de su característico color rojizo. Su atmósfera es muy delgada y se compone aproximadamente de un 95% de dióxido de carbono, además de nitrógeno y argón, con pequeñas cantidades de otros gases. Esta composición hace que el planeta no tenga aire respirable para los humanos y que no pueda mantener temperaturas adecuadas para la vida sin intervención tecnológica. Además, Marte presenta condiciones ambientales peligrosas: temperaturas extremadamente bajas, intensa radiación solar y cósmica, tormentas de polvo y una presión atmosférica muy inferior a la de la Tierra. Por estas razones, cualquier misión humana necesitaría tecnología especializada para proporcionar oxígeno, agua, alimento, energía y protección. Estudiar estas características permite comprender los retos de la exploración de Marte y muestra por qué es crucial desarrollar una guía de supervivencia que establezca procedimientos, medidas preventivas y soluciones tecnológicas para proteger la vida humana.
index.html.Mars is a rocky planet that is one of th: Marte es un planeta rocoso, uno de los planetas interiores del Sistema Solar. Su aspecto rojizo se debe principalmente a la presencia de óxidos de hierro en su suelo y sus rocas.
index.html.Reddish due to iron oxides: Rojizo por los óxidos de hierro
index.html.Mars is composed primarily of chemical e:
Marte está compuesto principalmente por elementos químicos que forman los minerales, rocas y materiales de su superficie y su interior. Entre sus componentes más importantes están:
- Hierro (Fe): presente en minerales y óxidos de hierro, responsable de su color rojizo.
index.html.- Silicon (Si): a component of silicates: - Silicio (Si): componente de los silicatos, que forman gran parte de sus rocas.
index.html.- Oxygen (O): found mainly combined with: - Oxígeno (O): se encuentra sobre todo combinado con otros elementos en minerales y óxidos.
index.html.- Magnesium (Mg): a component of various: - Magnesio (Mg): componente de varios minerales presentes en la corteza.
index.html.- Aluminum (Al): present in different mi: - Aluminio (Al): presente en distintos minerales de las rocas marcianas.
index.html.- Sulfur (S): found in minerals such as: - Azufre (S): se encuentra en minerales como los sulfatos.

La atmósfera marciana no es respirable para los humanos. Su baja presión y su baja concentración de oxígeno hacen indispensable el uso de sistemas artificiales de soporte vital.
index.html.Like Earth, Mars has an internal structu:
Al igual que la Tierra, Marte tiene una estructura interna dividida en tres regiones principales:
1. Corteza: es la capa exterior sólida del planeta, formada por rocas y minerales. Su superficie contiene volcanes, cráteres, montañas y extensas llanuras.
2. Manto: situado bajo la corteza, se compone principalmente de materiales rocosos ricos en silicatos y minerales de hierro y magnesio.
3. Núcleo: es la región central del planeta, compuesta principalmente de hierro, níquel y elementos ligeros como el azufre.
Esta estructura permite entender cómo se formó Marte y cómo evolucionó geológicamente a lo largo de miles de millones de años.
index.html.Human survival on Mars presents a challe:
La supervivencia humana en Marte es un reto debido a varias condiciones naturales:
- Falta de oxígeno: la atmósfera contiene muy poco oxígeno disponible para respirar.
- Temperaturas extremas: pueden descender hasta aproximadamente −125 °C.
- Radiación: Marte carece de un campo magnético global fuerte y su delgada atmósfera protege poco de la radiación.
- Tormentas de polvo: pueden reducir la visibilidad y dañar paneles solares y equipos.
- Baja presión atmosférica: es un peligro para el cuerpo humano sin protección.
- Escasez de agua líquida: aunque existe agua, sobre todo en forma de hielo, obtenerla y procesarla requiere tecnología.
- Dificultad para producir alimentos: habría que construir instalaciones protegidas para cultivar plantas.
index.html.Systems needed to survive on Mars: Sistemas necesarios para sobrevivir en Marte
index.html.To establish a human presence on Mars, i: Para establecer una presencia humana en Marte sería necesario desarrollar sistemas tecnológicos capaces de mantener condiciones similares a las de la Tierra.
index.html.An astronaut suit is essential for human: El traje de astronauta es esencial para la supervivencia humana en Marte porque el planeta no tiene atmósfera respirable y presenta temperaturas extremas y radiación peligrosa. Funciona como un pequeño sistema personal de soporte vital: proporciona oxígeno, regula la temperatura corporal y mantiene la presión que necesita el cuerpo humano.
index.html.The suit also protects astronauts from d: El traje también protege a los astronautas del polvo, de partículas dañinas y de otros peligros ambientales, y les permite moverse, comunicarse y realizar actividades científicas fuera del hábitat. Sus guantes, casco y capas especiales están diseñados para dar seguridad y movilidad durante la exploración espacial.
index.html.Reduce exposure to hazardous particles: Reducir la exposición a partículas peligrosas
index.html.Provide electricity using solar panels o: Proporcionar electricidad con paneles solares u otras fuentes
index.html.Create safe living and working environme: Crear espacios seguros para vivir y trabajar
index.html.Importance of a survival guide on Mars: Importancia de una guía de supervivencia en Marte
index.html.A survival guide is essential for organi:
Una guía de supervivencia es esencial para organizar las actividades y establecer procedimientos que protejan la vida humana en un entorno tan distinto al de la Tierra. Su importancia reside en varios aspectos:
- Identificar los peligros ambientales y saber cómo prevenirlos.
- Establecer protocolos de emergencia ante fallos de los sistemas de soporte vital.
- Determinar cómo obtener, almacenar y administrar los recursos esenciales.
- Diseñar hábitats seguros que protejan de la radiación y las temperaturas extremas.
- Asegurar el suministro de oxígeno, agua, alimento y energía.
- Preparar a los astronautas para responder a situaciones inesperadas.
Una guía de este tipo no solo serviría para resolver problemas durante una misión, sino también para planear futuras colonias humanas y desarrollar tecnologías que permitan una estancia prolongada en Marte.
index.html.Mars presents one of the greatest challe: Marte representa uno de los mayores retos de la exploración espacial por sus condiciones geológicas, químicas y ambientales. Aunque posee algunas características similares a las de la Tierra, su atmósfera rica en dióxido de carbono, sus temperaturas extremadamente bajas, la radiación y la escasez de agua líquida hacen imposible la supervivencia humana sin tecnología especializada. Comprender su composición química, su estructura interna, su gravedad y sus condiciones ambientales permite identificar los principales riesgos que enfrentarían los astronautas. Por ello, desarrollar una guía de supervivencia es fundamental para establecer medidas de seguridad, aprovechar los recursos disponibles y diseñar sistemas de soporte vital que mantengan condiciones adecuadas para la vida. En conclusión, la posibilidad de habitar Marte dependerá de los avances científicos y tecnológicos, y de la capacidad de la humanidad para adaptarse a un entorno completamente distinto al de nuestro planeta.
index.html.Hello! Welcome to our Mars survival guid: ¡Hola! ¡Bienvenido a nuestra guía de supervivencia en Marte!

mars-survival.html.Guía de supervivencia para una misión co: Survival guide for a conceptual mission of one astronaut lasting 21 Martian sols.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. Its surface gravity is about 3.7 m/s², close to 38% of Earth's. This reduced gravity affects walking, load handling and the human body's response; there is still no long-duration human experience in Martian gravity.
mars-survival.html.La duración de un día marciano —un sol—: A Martian day, a sol, lasts 24 hours, 39 minutes and 35 seconds. The mission uses sols to schedule activities and record consumption.
mars-survival.html.Composición aproximada de la atmósfera m: Approximate composition of the Martian atmosphere
mars-survival.html.Porcentajes aproximados reportados por N: Approximate percentages reported by NASA/JPL; they can vary slightly with the source and measurement conditions.
mars-survival.html.Extremos ilustrativos citados en el mate: Illustrative extremes quoted in NASA/JPL material for specific conditions; they are not the range of any given site or day.
mars-survival.html.La atmósfera marciana está compuesta pri: The Martian atmosphere is mostly carbon dioxide. NASA reference data give about 95.3% CO₂, 2.7% nitrogen and 1.6% argon. Surface pressure is under 1% of Earth's mean pressure.
mars-survival.html.Esta atmósfera no es respirable para una: This atmosphere cannot be breathed, and no one can stay exposed to it without a pressurised system. The habitat, the rover and the EVA suit must keep a pressure and gas mix compatible with human life.
mars-survival.html.La baja presión exterior hace inviable u: The low outside pressure rules out ordinary clothing or an open cabin. Seals, windows, airlocks, fluid connections and cable penetrations all need inspection and leak tests. The design should include pressure sensors at more than one point and procedures to isolate compartments where the architecture allows.
mars-survival.html.Marte presenta grandes variaciones térmi: Mars has large temperature swings. NASA reports a mean surface temperature near −53 °C, with extremes that depend on latitude, season and local time. The thin atmosphere holds little heat.
mars-survival.html.Se producen remolinos de polvo y torment: Dust devils and local, regional and global storms occur. Dust can cut the sunlight reaching the panels, coat surfaces, affect mechanisms and limit visibility. A solar-based architecture must therefore plan for reduced generation, storage and the suspension of non-essential activities.
mars-survival.html.Marte carece de un campo magnético globa: Mars has no global magnetic field like Earth's and its atmosphere is thin, so the surface gives less protection from cosmic radiation and solar particle events than Earth's surface does. Exposure depends on solar activity, location, time and the shielding available.
mars-survival.html.La misión debe medir y registrar la dosi: The mission must measure and record dose with suitable instruments, limit exposure time and define a shelter with extra protection. A dose figure from another mission must not be used as if it were the exact limit for this stay.
mars-survival.html.Presión, temperatura y velocidad/direcci: Pressure, temperature and wind speed and direction.
mars-survival.html.Opacidad del polvo y radiación solar dis: Dust opacity and available solar radiation.
mars-survival.html.Dosis radiológica acumulada y alertas de: Accumulated radiation dose and solar particle alerts.
mars-survival.html.Imágenes del terreno, pendiente y obstác: Images of the terrain, slope and obstacles before routes are authorised.
mars-survival.html.El terreno puede incluir roca expuesta,: The terrain can include exposed rock, regolith, slopes, craters, dunes and deposits. Before routes are set, it needs mapping and an assessment of slope, stability, obstacles and places where the rover could get stuck.
mars-survival.html.Se ha detectado hielo de agua en el subs: Water ice has been detected underground and in the polar regions. Its presence and accessibility vary with location. Since no landing site has been selected yet, this guide does not assume usable ice next to the habitat.
mars-survival.html.no seleccionar coordenadas definitivas h: do not fix final coordinates until terrain safety, lighting, communications, resources and environmental risks have been compared.
mars-survival.html.La supervivencia depende de mantener una: Survival depends on keeping a controlled atmosphere. The system must watch total pressure, oxygen concentration, carbon dioxide, humidity, temperature and contaminants. A loss of pressure or an out-of-limits atmosphere calls for an immediate response and procedures validated in advance.
mars-survival.html.El oxígeno puede almacenarse y distribui: Oxygen can be stored and distributed from reserves, and a life support system can produce it by electrolysis. The MOXIE demonstration on the Perseverance rover produced a total of 122 grams of oxygen during its operations; at its best it reached about 12 grams per hour at a purity of at least 98%. It was an intermittent technology demonstration, not a continuous plant able to supply a crew. In this conceptual mission, oxygen must therefore be sized with its own storage and support systems; MOXIE serves only as a proof of principle for using local resources.
mars-survival.html.Para la planificación preliminar se habí: Preliminary planning used a metabolic reference of 0.84 kg of O₂ per person per Earth day. Over 21 sols that is about 18.1 kg nominal, before margins, losses, physical activity and system design. This value must be validated against the real activity profile and the life support architecture.
mars-survival.html.Escala de referencia: oxígeno para la es: Reference scale: oxygen for the stay
mars-survival.html.Consumo nominal estimado para 21 soles,: Estimated nominal consumption for 21 sols, at 0.84 kg per Earth day
mars-survival.html.Producción total acumulada por MOXIE en: Total oxygen produced by MOXIE on Mars
mars-survival.html.Comparación de escala, no de tecnología: A comparison of scale, not of equivalent technology: the mission's estimated consumption is about 148 times MOXIE's total production. The consumption figure is a planning assumption and includes no margins, losses or reserves.
mars-survival.html.El astronauta exhala CO₂. El sistema de: The astronaut breathes out CO₂. The air revitalisation system must remove it to prevent a dangerous build-up, control contaminants and keep the air circulating evenly. NASA describes CO₂ removal and monitoring systems within ECLSS.
mars-survival.html.El agua es necesaria para beber, prepara: Water is needed for drinking, preparing food, hygiene and operations. The space station recovers wastewater, humidity condensate and other streams to produce reusable water after filtration and treatment.
mars-survival.html.La recuperación reduce la cantidad que d: Recovery reduces what must be carried, but it does not remove the need for reserves. NASA states that the station's water recovery system recycles about 90% in operation; in 2023 NASA reported that up to 98% total recovery had been demonstrated with the brine processor added. That 98% is a milestone demonstrated on the ISS, not a guarantee for a Mars system. Water quality must be verified, and losses, filters, brine, maintenance and water held in food must be accounted for.
mars-survival.html.La cifra preliminar de 3.56 kg por perso: The preliminary figure of 3.56 kg per person per day is a reference flow for planning, not the net mass that must be carried. The real load depends on the recovery rate demonstrated by the chosen system.
mars-survival.html.Recuperación de agua: referencia de la E: Water recovery: International Space Station reference
mars-survival.html.Hito demostrado con procesador de salmue: Milestone demonstrated with the brine processor
mars-survival.html.Referencia tecnológica de la ISS. No es: ISS technology reference. It is not a guaranteed performance for Mars and does not replace this mission's balance of losses and reserves.
mars-survival.html.Los alimentos de la misión deben cubrir: Mission food must cover energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, fibre, vitamins and minerals, with stable storage and preparation suited to the habitat. For a 21-sol stay, carried food is the main source; an experimental crop must not be counted as a critical supply.
mars-survival.html.La estimación preliminar de 0.62 kg de a: The preliminary estimate of 0.62 kg of food per day is a logistics assumption, not a validated diet. It must be replaced by a nutrition plan designed for the person, the activity and the storage.
mars-survival.html.2.6 Salud física, mental y rutina: 2.6 Physical health, mental health and routine
mars-survival.html.La rutina debe incluir sueño, ejercicio,: The routine must include sleep, exercise, food, hygiene, maintenance and recovery time. Martian gravity is partial, and its long-term effect on the human body is not yet known. Bone-loss percentages seen in microgravity must not be carried over to Mars automatically.
mars-survival.html.El aislamiento, la carga de trabajo, la: Isolation, workload, communication with Earth and monotony can affect performance. Planning must provide regular hours, varied tasks, scheduled communication and procedures for fatigue or stress.
mars-survival.html.El seguimiento debe registrar, como míni: Monitoring must record at least sleep, workload, hydration, intake, exercise, symptoms, injuries and functional capacity. Medical protocols must be defined by professionals and tied to specific equipment and medicines; this guide sets no clinical thresholds and does not replace a medical assessment.
mars-survival.html.Un traje espacial funciona como un siste: A spacesuit works as a personal life support system: it supplies pressure and oxygen, removes CO₂, controls temperature and humidity, provides power and allows communication. Before each outing, check its integrity, autonomy, communications, mobility and fit with the airlock or access port.
mars-survival.html.O₂ ≈ 18.1 kg nominales; agua ≈ 76.8 kg d: O₂ ≈ 18.1 kg nominal; water ≈ 76.8 kg reference flow; CO₂ generated ≈ 21.6 kg to process; food ≈ 13.4 kg under the 0.62 kg/day assumption. These are not final loads and do not replace system sizing.
mars-survival.html.La arquitectura acordada contempla dos r: The agreed architecture has two pressurised shelters:
mars-survival.html.. No se incluye un tercer refugio ni un: . This version includes no third shelter and no independent rescue vehicle.
mars-survival.html.El hábitat fijo será el centro de vida y: The fixed habitat is the centre of life and operations. The rover serves as a pressurised mobile vehicle and as an alternative shelter only when its pressure, life support, power and access systems are working.
mars-survival.html.Estructura presurizada y protección cont: Pressurised structure and protection from the outside environment.
mars-survival.html.Esclusa para entrada y salida con contro: Airlock for entry and exit with dust control.
mars-survival.html.Sistema ECLSS para presión, oxígeno, ven: ECLSS for pressure, oxygen, ventilation, CO₂, water and waste.
mars-survival.html.Control térmico, distribución eléctrica: Thermal control, power distribution and lighting.
mars-survival.html.Comunicaciones, computación, almacenamie: Communications, computing, storage and environmental monitoring.
mars-survival.html.Área médica, alimentos, herramientas y r: Medical area, food, tools and spares.
mars-survival.html.Duplicar una pieza no garantiza redundan: Duplicating a part does not give redundancy if both units share the same power feed, controller, wiring or cooling loop. Critical systems must be isolable and keep essential functions through independent paths where technically possible.
mars-survival.html.Se deben considerar sensores redundantes: Consider redundant sensors, backup controllers, spare fans and pumps, separable electrical circuits and emergency oxygen storage. The exact architecture needs a failure analysis and detailed design.
mars-survival.html.El rover debe tener cabina presurizada,: The rover needs a pressurised cabin, its own life support, power, thermal control, navigation and communications. The preliminary proposal has a reference habitable volume of 10–12 m³ and a normal autonomy of 2–3 sols; both are conceptual targets to be verified through mass, volume and consumption design and testing.
mars-survival.html.El acceso tipo suitport puede reducir el: A suitport can reduce the dust entering the rover, but it must be studied together with a conventional emergency route. An immobilised rover does not count as an available shelter if it cannot keep pressure, life support and power.
mars-survival.html.Prueba de estanqueidad y estabilidad de: Leak test and cabin pressure stability.
mars-survival.html.Verificación de suministro de oxígeno y: Check of oxygen supply and CO₂ removal.
mars-survival.html.Comprobación de energía disponible, temp: Check of available power, temperature and ventilation.
mars-survival.html.Prueba de comunicaciones, navegación y r: Test of communications, navigation and return to the habitat.
mars-survival.html.Confirmación de que el sistema de acceso: Confirmation that the access system can be operated from inside and outside as designed.
mars-survival.html.El hábitat y el rover deben mantener tem: The habitat and the rover must keep internal temperatures suitable for people and equipment, using insulation, heating, heat rejection and monitoring. Dust can contaminate seals, filters, radiators and mechanisms; cleaning and maintenance must be part of the design.
mars-survival.html.el hábitat fijo y el rover no deben comp: the fixed habitat and the rover must not share a single critical dependency that could disable both shelters at once.
mars-survival.html.La exploración se realizará con tres med: Exploration uses three means: the pressurised rover, autonomous robots and EVA on foot. The choice depends on risk, distance, terrain, suit autonomy, rover condition and the environment.
mars-survival.html.Reconocimiento cercano con robots y EVA: Close reconnaissance with robots and short EVA, within safety limits.
mars-survival.html.Exploración con rover y robots auxiliare: Exploration with the rover and support robots.
mars-survival.html.Desplazamiento con rover presurizado y p: Travel by pressurised rover with a planned return.
mars-survival.html.En la primera etapa, reconocimiento robó: In the first stage, robotic reconnaissance; no human outing of that range is authorised until autonomy, shelter and safe return are demonstrated.
mars-survival.html.Una ruta debe incluir distancia de ida y: A route must include the out-and-back distance, climb, slope, ground type, obstacles, low-visibility areas, energy, time, communication points and alternatives. A destination 20 km away means at least 40 km there and back, before detours.
mars-survival.html.Datos que debe contener cada plan de sal: What every outing plan must contain
mars-survival.html.Identificador de ruta, objetivo y duraci: Route identifier, objective and estimated duration.
mars-survival.html.Distancia total, desnivel, pendientes y: Total distance, climb, slopes and surface.
mars-survival.html.Consumo energético del rover y autonomía: Rover energy use and suit autonomy.
mars-survival.html.Pronóstico de polvo, temperatura, ilumin: Forecast of dust, temperature, lighting and radiation.
mars-survival.html.Puntos de retorno, refugio alternativo y: Turn-back points, alternative shelter and abort limits.
mars-survival.html.Estado del robot de apoyo y canal de com: Status of the support robot and the communications channel.
mars-survival.html.Los robots pueden realizar reconocimient: Robots can do advance reconnaissance, mapping, terrain inspection, tool transport and data collection. Autonomy reduces human exposure, but robots can also fail through power, navigation, communications, dust or mechanical damage.
mars-survival.html.Una EVA requiere autorización previa, re: An EVA needs prior authorisation, a suit check, a communications check, an environmental forecast, an approved route and confirmation of a reachable shelter. An abort criterion must exist before the outing starts and throughout the activity.
mars-survival.html.La distancia entre la Tierra y Marte gen: The distance between Earth and Mars causes variable communication delays, so immediate safety decisions cannot depend on a real-time answer from Earth. The local system must detect dangerous conditions and carry out pre-approved safe procedures.
mars-survival.html.el rover debe permanecer a una distancia: the rover must stay at a distance and in a condition that let the astronaut reach a pressurised shelter within the suit's real, validated autonomy. A universal rescue time must not be invented.
mars-survival.html.. No se incluye un reactor nuclear en es: . This version includes no nuclear reactor. This is a project architecture decision, not a claim that solar power is the most robust option in all Martian conditions.
mars-survival.html.El presupuesto conceptual utiliza una po: The conceptual budget uses a mean power of 10 kW for the habitat, thermal control, computing, communications, lighting, laboratory, robotics and rover services. Held for 21 sols (about 517.86 Earth hours), the total energy would be close to 5,179 kWh.
mars-survival.html.La distribución por subsistema y la dema: The split by subsystem and the real demand must be refined with specific equipment, usage profiles, start-ups, power peaks and conversion losses.
mars-survival.html.Distribución hipotética del presupuesto: Hypothetical split of the 10 kW budget agreed for the project. It must be replaced by real equipment loads and hourly profiles.
mars-survival.html.Energía para 21 soles a 10 kW constantes: Energy for 21 sols at a constant 10 kW
mars-survival.html.El dimensionamiento inicial propuso 356: Initial sizing proposed 356 m² of panels. That result depends on assumptions about irradiance, efficiency, losses, orientation, latitude, season and dust. It must not be treated as a guaranteed capacity until a site is selected and local environmental data are used.
mars-survival.html.Se propusieron 514 kWh nominales para un: 514 kWh nominal were proposed as an emergency reserve for the central system. This preliminary figure does not include the rover's traction battery and must be reviewed to avoid counting night-time energy and emergency reserve twice. Usable capacity depends on depth of discharge, temperature, ageing and efficiency.
mars-survival.html.Una tormenta de polvo puede reducir la g: A dust storm can cut photovoltaic generation for long periods. The system must provide for generation monitoring, field isolation, storage, load shedding, EVA suspension and priority for life support. Do not assume the wind will clean the panels by itself.
mars-survival.html.Presión, oxígeno, eliminación de CO₂ y c: Pressure, oxygen, CO₂ removal and vital thermal control.
mars-survival.html.Exploración y desplazamientos cuando exi: Exploration and travel when there is an energy margin.
mars-survival.html.los 10 kW, 356 m² y 514 kWh son parámetr: the 10 kW, 356 m² and 514 kWh are study parameters of this project. They do not describe a Martian solar system already built or validated by NASA.
mars-survival.html.Selecciona el sol, el modo de operación: Select the sol, the operating mode and one or more failures. Running the simulation updates the demonstration indicators and adds an entry to the log.
mars-survival.html.este simulador recupera la lógica demost: this simulator reuses the demonstration logic of the first prototype. The percentages are a simplified response to the scenario; they are not certified physical, medical or engineering predictions.
mars-survival.html.Puedes seleccionar una o varias fallas s: You can select one or several failures at once.
mars-survival.html.Selecciona un sol y, si lo deseas, intro: Select a sol and, if you wish, introduce failures to assess the scenario.
mars-survival.html.Sistema preparado. La simulación aún no: System ready. The simulation has not started yet.
mars-survival.html.Se conserva el último registro de cada s: The last record for each sol is kept during this browser session.
mars-survival.html.Selecciona una problemática para despleg: Select a problem to show the planned response. The solutions are conceptual criteria for action; before a real mission they would have to become approved, trained and tested procedures for the specific equipment.
mars-survival.html.Proteger la vida del astronauta: presión: Protect the astronaut's life: pressure, oxygen, CO₂, temperature and physical condition.
mars-survival.html.Conservar al menos un refugio presurizad: Keep at least one pressurised shelter reachable.
mars-survival.html.Mantener soporte vital y energía esencia: Maintain life support and essential power.
mars-survival.html.Recuperar al astronauta y retornar al re: Recover the astronaut and return to the safe shelter.
mars-survival.html.Restablecer comunicaciones y evaluar la: Restore communications and assess whether the mission can continue.
mars-survival.html.Reanudar ciencia y exploración únicament: Resume science and exploration only after safety margins are recovered.
mars-survival.html.01 · Pérdida de presión en el hábitat: 01 · Loss of pressure in the habitat
mars-survival.html.Una fuga en la estructura, una junta, un: A leak in the structure, a seal, a hatch or a connection can lower the internal pressure and compromise the breathable atmosphere.
mars-survival.html.Activar la alarma y confirmar la tendenc: Raise the alarm and confirm the trend with independent sensors.
mars-survival.html.Detener actividades no esenciales y loca: Stop non-essential activities and locate the affected compartment.
mars-survival.html.Aislar el volumen dañado si el diseño di: Isolate the damaged volume if the design has isolation doors or valves.
mars-survival.html.Si la presión continúa cayendo o el comp: If pressure keeps falling or the compartment is not safe, move to the other pressurised shelter only if the route and the alternative system have been verified.
mars-survival.html.Localizar y reparar la fuga con un proce: Find and repair the leak with an approved procedure, run a leak test and check the atmosphere's composition before reoccupying the compartment.
mars-survival.html.Presión estable, fuga aislada o reparada: Stable pressure, leak isolated or repaired, sensors in agreement and life support working. Do not improvise structural patches without design and testing.
mars-survival.html.Puede fallar el generador, una válvula,: The generator, a valve, a regulator, a distribution line or a sensor can fail. Oxygen concentration could stop being held within the habitat's operating range.
mars-survival.html.Confirmar la lectura con sensores redund: Confirm the reading with redundant sensors.
mars-survival.html.Activar la reserva de oxígeno diseñada p: Activate the oxygen reserve designed for emergencies.
mars-survival.html.Aislar el componente o circuito defectuo: Isolate the faulty component or circuit if it is safe to do so.
mars-survival.html.Reducir actividades y preparar el trasla: Reduce activity and prepare to move to the alternative shelter if the supply cannot be stabilised.
mars-survival.html.Identificar si la falla está en producci: Identify whether the fault is in production, storage or distribution; switch to the redundant line or replace the component by procedure, and check the quality of the atmosphere.
mars-survival.html.Reserva suficiente, suministro estable,: Sufficient reserve, stable supply, redundant measurement and confirmed life support capacity.
mars-survival.html.Un filtro agotado, una bomba detenida, u: A spent filter, a stopped pump, a closed valve or a circulation fault can prevent removal of the CO₂ the astronaut breathes out.
mars-survival.html.Confirmar la lectura con un segundo sens: Confirm the reading with a second sensor and check air circulation.
mars-survival.html.Activar el equipo de eliminación de CO₂: Activate the redundant CO₂ removal equipment or the planned backup cartridge.
Reduce physical effort and suspend EVA.
mars-survival.html.Si no se recupera el control, trasladars: If control is not recovered, move to the shelter with a working air system.
mars-survival.html.Reemplazar el medio filtrante o reparar: Replace the filter medium or repair the circuit; check flow, sensors and the concentration trend before returning to normal operation.
mars-survival.html.CO₂ controlado por el sistema validado,: CO₂ controlled by the validated system, working sensors and backup capacity available.
mars-survival.html.04 · Tormenta de polvo y caída de genera: 04 · Dust storm and drop in solar generation
mars-survival.html.El polvo suspendido y depositado puede r: Suspended and settled dust can cut the energy reaching the panels, limit visibility and affect mechanisms or filters.
mars-survival.html.Comparar generación real con pronóstico: Compare real generation with the forecast and estimate battery autonomy.
mars-survival.html.Pasar a cargas esenciales: soporte vital: Switch to essential loads: life support, thermal control, sensors and minimum communications.
mars-survival.html.Aislar campos eléctricos dañados si corr: Isolate damaged electrical fields where needed and protect exposed equipment.
mars-survival.html.Inspeccionar los paneles cuando las cond: Inspect the panels when conditions are safe; use only cleaning methods that were designed and tested. Do not assume the wind will clean the panels, and do not activate improvised mechanisms.
mars-survival.html.Generación suficiente o reserva energéti: Sufficient generation or an energy reserve confirmed for the expected duration, plus acceptable visibility and mobility conditions.
mars-survival.html.Una batería puede perder capacidad, desc: A battery can lose capacity, disconnect, overheat or stop delivering power. The failure can affect the habitat or the rover.
mars-survival.html.Identificar qué banco o circuito está af: Identify which bank or circuit is affected.
mars-survival.html.Aislar el banco defectuoso si el sistema: Isolate the faulty bank if the protection system commands it.
mars-survival.html.Transferir cargas a un circuito independ: Transfer loads to an independent circuit only if it was designed for that.
mars-survival.html.Desconectar cargas no esenciales y prote: Disconnect non-essential loads and protect life support and thermal control first.
mars-survival.html.Evaluar temperatura, voltaje, aislamient: Assess temperature, voltage, insulation and remaining capacity; do not reconnect a battery showing signs of thermal or electrical damage until the technical inspection is complete.
mars-survival.html.Potencia y autonomía verificadas para el: Power and autonomy verified for the selected operating scenario, including the reserve margin.
mars-survival.html.06 · Rover inmovilizado o con daño en un: 06 · Rover immobilised or with a damaged wheel
mars-survival.html.Una rueda, motor, suspensión o sistema d: A wheel, motor, suspension or traction system can be damaged and leave the rover stopped far from the habitat.
mars-survival.html.Detener el movimiento y evaluar estabili: Stop moving and assess the vehicle's stability and the state of the cabin.
mars-survival.html.Comprobar si el rover mantiene presión,: Check whether the rover is keeping pressure, life support, power and communications.
mars-survival.html.Si el astronauta está fuera, seguir el p: If the astronaut is outside, follow the plan to return to the reachable shelter; do not assume the rover is safe just because the cabin is intact.
mars-survival.html.Evitar maniobras que puedan volcar o agr: Avoid manoeuvres that could tip the rover or worsen the damage.
mars-survival.html.Usar diagnóstico a bordo, teleoperación: Use on-board diagnostics, teleoperation or the repair provided for by design. If it cannot be recovered, set an alternative route only with confirmed resources, autonomy and shelter.
mars-survival.html.Prueba funcional de movilidad, frenado,: Functional test of mobility, braking, navigation and life support; otherwise the rover stays out of service.
mars-survival.html.07 · Falla de navegación o pérdida de co: 07 · Navigation failure or loss of communications
mars-survival.html.El rover o los robots pueden perder posi: The rover or the robots can lose positioning, reliable maps or the communication link with the habitat or Earth.
mars-survival.html.Detener el movimiento autónomo si la pos: Stop autonomous movement if the position or route is not reliable.
mars-survival.html.Conservar la última posición validada y: Keep the last validated position and compare independent sensors.
mars-survival.html.Usar navegación local y procedimientos p: Use local navigation and pre-programmed procedures; do not depend on an instant answer from Earth.
mars-survival.html.Abortar la exploración si no puede demos: Abort the exploration if a safe return route cannot be demonstrated.
mars-survival.html.Restablecer antena o enlace, reconstruir: Restore the antenna or link, rebuild the position with the sensors available and verify the route before allowing movement. The AI may recommend, but it must not override safety limits.
mars-survival.html.Posición consistente, comunicaciones mín: Consistent position, minimum communications working or a validated autonomous mode, and a verified return route.
mars-survival.html.Una fuga, pérdida de presión, falla de o: A leak, loss of pressure, or a failure of oxygen, CO₂ removal, thermal control, power or communication can put the astronaut at immediate risk.
mars-survival.html.Abortar la actividad y activar el proced: Abort the activity and start the suit's specific emergency procedure.
mars-survival.html.Dirigirse al refugio presurizado accesib: Head for the reachable pressurised shelter by the established return route and method.
mars-survival.html.Solicitar asistencia local y mantener co: Request local assistance and keep communicating if the system still works.
mars-survival.html.No continuar la tarea científica ni desv: Do not continue the science task or detour to recover tools or samples.
mars-survival.html.Una vez dentro del refugio, estabilizar: Once inside the shelter, stabilise the astronaut under the approved medical and technical protocol; isolate the suit and download its records for diagnosis.
mars-survival.html.El traje debe ser reparado, probado y au: The suit must be repaired, tested and authorised again. If autonomy or the reachable shelter is not confirmed, the EVA does not start.
mars-survival.html.09 · Sobrecalentamiento o pérdida de con: 09 · Overheating or loss of thermal control
mars-survival.html.Una bomba, ventilador, radiador, sensor: A pump, fan, radiator, sensor or thermal circuit can fail and cause temperatures outside the range allowed for people or equipment.
mars-survival.html.Confirmar lecturas con sensores redundan: Confirm readings with redundant sensors and locate the affected circuit.
mars-survival.html.Activar el circuito de respaldo si está: Activate the backup circuit if it is available and isolated.
mars-survival.html.Si el hábitat deja de ser seguro, trasla: If the habitat is no longer safe, move to the alternative shelter only if it keeps thermal conditions and life support.
mars-survival.html.Reparar o aislar el circuito, verificar: Repair or isolate the circuit, check circulation and heat rejection, and stabilise the environment before restoring the normal load.
mars-survival.html.Temperaturas estables, sensores confiabl: Stable temperatures, reliable sensors and thermal redundancy restored, or a formally authorised degraded plan.
mars-survival.html.Un evento de partículas solares puede el: A solar particle event can raise radiation exposure, especially during activities outside a protected shelter.
mars-survival.html.Recibir y evaluar las alertas de monitor: Receive and assess the solar monitoring alerts available.
mars-survival.html.Suspender EVA y retornar al refugio con: Suspend EVA and return to the shelter with the most protection available.
mars-survival.html.Reducir el tiempo en zonas con blindaje: Reduce time in areas with limited shielding and record the exposure.
mars-survival.html.Seguir el procedimiento de protección ra: Follow the mission's radiation protection and medical assessment procedure.
mars-survival.html.Revisar datos de dosímetros, estado del: Review dosimeter data, the state of the event and the medical assessment before authorising outside activities.
mars-survival.html.Autorización basada en mediciones, pronó: Authorisation based on measurements, forecast and the radiation criteria set for the mission; no universal threshold is invented.
mars-survival.html.11 · Falla de suministro, recuperación o: 11 · Water supply, recovery or contamination failure
mars-survival.html.Una fuga, bomba, filtro o etapa de trata: A leak, pump, filter or treatment stage can interrupt the supply or produce water that does not meet the quality criteria.
mars-survival.html.Aislar el circuito sospechoso y conserva: Isolate the suspect circuit and keep the safe stored water.
mars-survival.html.Verificar calidad con los sensores y pru: Check quality with the planned sensors and tests; do not drink water of doubtful quality.
mars-survival.html.Priorizar agua potable y usos esenciales: Give priority to drinking water and essential uses; suspend non-critical uses.
mars-survival.html.Activar el circuito de tratamiento o res: Activate the alternative treatment circuit or reserve if it is validated.
mars-survival.html.Localizar la fuga o etapa defectuosa, su: Find the leak or faulty stage, replace filters or repair pumps, reprocess the water and confirm its quality before returning it to the service tank.
mars-survival.html.Agua verificada, inventario suficiente y: Verified water, sufficient inventory and treatment or reserve capacity restored.
mars-survival.html.El robot puede perder energía, movilidad: The robot can lose power, mobility, navigation, sensors or communication and fail to complete its task.
mars-survival.html.Detener órdenes de movimiento si existe: Stop movement commands if there is a risk of collision or loss of control.
mars-survival.html.Guardar la última telemetría y posición: Save the last telemetry and known position.
mars-survival.html.No enviar al astronauta a recuperarlo si: Do not send the astronaut to recover it if the operation compromises a safety route or reserve.
mars-survival.html.Intentar diagnóstico remoto y reinicio s: Attempt remote diagnosis and restart only if the procedure allows it; plan physical recovery in a safe window or declare the equipment lost.
mars-survival.html.El robot supera pruebas de sensores, nav: The robot passes sensor, navigation, communications and mobility tests before operating again near people or critical equipment.
mars-survival.html.7.3 Fallas simultáneas y límites de recu: 7.3 Simultaneous failures and limits of recovery
mars-survival.html.Una falla combinada puede superar la cap: A combined failure can exceed the capacity to respond. For example, if the suit is compromised, the rover is immobilised and no other pressurised shelter is reachable, the current architecture may offer no recovery. This case must be treated as a design risk that requires prevention, not as a situation artificial intelligence can solve by itself.
mars-survival.html.La causa de la falla está identificada o: The cause of the failure is identified or isolated.
mars-survival.html.El astronauta se encuentra estable y el: The astronaut is stable and the shelter is safe.
mars-survival.html.Soporte vital, energía y comunicaciones: Life support, power and communications have sufficient capacity.
mars-survival.html.La redundancia necesaria está disponible: The necessary redundancy is available or an approved degraded operation exists.
mars-survival.html.La ruta, el equipo y los criterios de ab: The route, the equipment and the abort criteria have been reviewed.
mars-survival.html.esta sección es una base de análisis con: this section is a basis for conceptual analysis. It is not a certified flight, medical or rescue procedure; each solution must become a specific checklist validated for the real hardware.
